core_obligations: Take the generic points of the fibre specialising to x and show their component dimensions agree using the Cohen-Macaulay criterion and openness (proof lines 6295-6310).

Use flatness of the single cohomology sheaf to compute its pullback to the fibre and identify it with the dualizing complex, concluding via the Cohen-Macaulay criterion for dualizing complexes (proof lines 6310-6319).
proof_roadmap: The generic points and the equality of dimensions (proof lines 6295-6310).
The pullback to the fibre and the dualizing complex (proof lines 6310-6316).
Cohen-Macaulayness of the fibre and conclusion (proof lines 6316-6319).
difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for f : X -> Y a morphism of FTS_S and a point x in X at which f is flat, the lemma asserts the equivalence of f being Cohen-Macaulay at x and f^!O_Y having a unique nonzero cohomology sheaf in a neighbourhood of x (statement lines 6283-6293). One direction is Lemma labelled lemma-CM-shriek; for the converse the proof assumes the unique cohomology sheaf and lets y = f(x), xi_1, ..., xi_n be the generic points of the fibre X_y specialising to x with d_1, ..., d_n the dimensions of the corresponding components (proof lines 6295-6304). The morphism is Cohen-Macaulay at each xi_i by More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-open, so by Lemma labelled lemma-CM-shriek all the d_i are equal, say to d, and d = dim_x(X_y); after shrinking X one may assume all fibres have dimension at most d by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres (proof lines 6306-6310). Then the only nonzero cohomology sheaf omega = H^{-d}(f^!O_Y) is flat over Y by Lemma labelled lemma-flat-shriek, so for the canonical morphism h : X_y -> X one has Lh^*(f^!O_Y) = (h^*omega)[d] by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-tor-independence-and-tor-amplitude (proof lines 6312-6316). By Lemma labelled lemma-relative-dualizing-fibres this is the dualizing complex of X_y, hence X_y is Cohen-Macaulay by Lemma labelled lemma-dualizing-module-CM-scheme, which gives the claim (proof lines 6316-6319). Comparing the dimensions of the components through the Cohen-Macaulay locus and then reading Cohen-Macaulayness of the fibre off its dualizing complex is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
